# Shared dependency, conflict and adversarial design review

Spec-only review at `d51222ffbb7e3eb6d08fed394851a52de3f5522c`, `recipe-view-redesign`, 2026-11-07. No main-capability sync, archive, product changes, commits or production execution. Implementation checkboxes remain unchecked. The follow-up decision reconciliation was prepared from clean `recipe-view-redesign` at `482d44731ab44ec703f70e1252751fc0964bf7f2`. Alex subsequently approved the product rules recorded below; the initial source review remains historical evidence. A structurally valid OpenSpec draft is not implementation approval or tested product behavior.

## Ownership and dependency graph

| Review unit | Owns | Depends on / can release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| canonical-ingredient-correction | Exact original rows/basis/steps, contentRevision, protected publication, common DTO/editor and canonical projector input | Foundation; never a competing replacement schema |
| restore-dependable-grocery-interactions | Row/check identity, guarded check/bulk operations, reset comparison, no review acknowledgement, focus and category-control interaction | Reusable legacy demand identity can ship before full canonical migration; client fence and fresh-list/history-preservation upgrade required |
| bilingual-shopping-identity | Saved app food IDs/EN-FR labels, aliases, shopping grouping/units, category scope/provenance | Canonical saved association and grocery row identity; no dictionary-completeness dependency for step scaling |
| scale-cooking-step-ingredients | Revision-bound uses, allocation/rendering, original step editing, coherent cooking refresh and prepared current-recipe reading | Canonical facts; mandatory for complete portions release, independent of dictionary coverage |
| migrate-canonical-recipe-model | In-place conversion, conditional fallback, old-writer fencing, fresh-list upgrade preserving history and complete current-format recovery | Design begins now; activation requires final persisted contracts of all owners |

All proposed shapes live in [contracts.md](contracts.md). Every delta requirement is owned once across this set; this includes moving canonical draft cooking/grocery/recovery deltas into companions. Existing main specs remain implementation baselines until a separately approved apply/sync. No duplicate “recipe facts v2” capability is created.

Read projection chain: original canonical rows/basis + one content revision → existing context resolver → ingredient/step projection → Home/detail/Cook and ingredient demand-only grocery aggregation → saved food/fallback + compatible unit bucket → stable weekly row → row check. Step use is an allocation, never another supply. Recipe row ID, step ID, food ID, grocery row ID, extra occurrence ID and prepared occurrence ID are different keys.

## Source-grounded conflicts and disposition

| Existing owner/evidence | Conflict or unintended effect | Required disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RecipeService.UpdateRecipe / SupperIngredientProjection.Read | String Save invalidates retained measured supply; old ingredient-only revision misses instruction races | Foundation: exact rows + content-wide guard; no positional transfer; source stays evidence |
| SupperIngredientProjection.IntentionallyUnquantified | Phrase whitelist can misclassify “Fresh basil leaves” | Foundation permits unknown amount/unit independently; no required phrase or automatic report |
| cooking / Explain original instruction amounts during scaling; old canonical Preserve original instructions | Explicitly mandates unchanged step quantities and blanket limitation note | Step delta replaces it with validated projection and selective quiet uncertainty |
| supper-servings / Scale each usable ingredient; Report incomplete scaling | Prohibits text scaling and retains grocery prior-unknown warning references | Step delta retains protection for unrelated text and removes stale warning cross-reference; foundation retains projection context owner |
| cooking / Apply a successful step edit locally | Submitted-array local install could mix new text with old binding/amount revision | Install returned coherent content, original draft and guard; no projected Save |
| cooking / Return from quality reporting | Applying report response recipe immediately can mix changed semantic content during active cooking | Apply report metadata; changed content enters explicit coherent refresh, preserve reporting trigger |
| GroceryRecomputeService and grocery-shopping shared display-name checks | Different bucket rows share a key | Grocery delta replaces name/bulk API assumptions, coordination and snapshots together |
| GroceryList.mutateExtra success callback | Unconditional Edit focus after checkbox mutation causes jumping | Checkbox/edit-specific focus contracts; preserve scroll on sort and future-extra disappearance |
| grocery-shopping prior_amount_unknown and source-disclosure requirements | Review copy/state can survive even if one string is removed | Remove marker generation, DTO/ack handling and both-locale UI; reconcile all adjacent source/subtotal requirements |
| IngredientNormalizer and categorization raw supply | Full description aliases can merge wrong foods or ignore corrections | Saved reviewed identity + fallback, no runtime AI; keep purchase qualifiers and human category priority |
| UnitNormalizer 240/15/5 ml culinary defaults, generic piece family | Regional and count-kind meanings currently collapse | No unproven standard migration; explicit units/count kinds, impact manifests and separate unresolved buckets |
| RecipeAgent file output → SyncRecipeProcessor | Existing reimport can replace raw instructions/basis before human guard | Stage file and DB publication; captured source/content revisions and protected fields are mandatory for preserved report-triggered repair |
| data-backup-and-recovery legacy arrays/version1/absent artifacts | Permanent old backup support contradicts chosen current-only model | Migration delta changes ordinary restore/sync preflight and all affected absent/history/serving/report/extra requirements; bounded one-time source converter is separate |
| Current-format merge | Format version does not prove newer content; opaque revisions not orderable | Ancestry/protection reconciliation; identical-token divergent bytes invalid; explicit exact replacement remains separate |
| Prepared reading | Frozen count can be confused with frozen recipe/basis | Current content at recorded count; preserve actual preparation/receipt/date and cooked-baseline contract; never claim historical recipe snapshot |
| Future CI defaults / uncommitted parity work | Name “CI” or all-suite selector does not itself prove production/real DB coverage | Depend on parity owner and explicit suite/live prerequisites below; no CI edits here |

Current report/repair evidence: `RecipeController` exposes POST/DELETE `/api/recipes/{id}/import-report`; `RecipeImportReportService.SubmitAsync` persists feedback first, reuses matching active attempts, blocks changed active feedback, avoids unchanged terminal relaunch and starts eligible URL/photo workflows only with nonblank content feedback and no Duplicate. Attempt-linked success/failure preserves reports. Demo AI/quota/recovery rules stay intact. The old proposed `/ingredient-repair` candidate workflow is absent from OpenAPI; its five tasks were unchecked. It is marked superseded/unimplemented in place, not archived or promoted. Retiring that proposal does not remove existing flags or repair triggers.

Current report locking is explicitly in-process; the new design cannot claim replica-wide safe deduplication from that fact. Before enabling multiple replicas, durable attempt/publication coordination must be designed and qualified separately. Preserve current single-instance boundary now.

## Proposed engineering choices and tradeoffs

- Rational string transport avoids JS precision loss and binary fraction drift; bounded input/intermediates prevent pathological arithmetic. Costs: tagged DTO migration, locale grammar and property fixtures. AmountText is validated notation, never a second numeric authority.
- Revision-bound spans fit existing plain-text editing; segments could be safer for rich editing but expand scope. UTF-16 boundary validation, expected substrings and exact revisions are required; stale spans stay readable and unscaled.
- Conservative fallback names and a curated identity seed avoid speculative bilingual merges. Costs: less aggregation and incomplete translation, acceptable with honest source labels. No upstream dataset has demonstrated corpus fit yet.
- Alex approved new split/merge rows starting unchecked rather than inheriting purchase intent. Continuing checked rows compare current requirement against a persisted checked-demand baseline, never the preceding recomputation; preserved overlaps/decreases do not advance it.
- Complete current-format manifest…253 tokens truncated…
3. Rows newly created by split or merge start unchecked. Unchanged continuing rows keep checks subject to the approved proven-increase rule; label/locale changes do not imply a new row.
4. Alex confirms no active grocery list during upgrade and says the next list will be new. New recipe-derived rows start unchecked with no inherited old-name checks/baselines. Preserve historical list/check data and extra occurrences/history; do not reinterpret ambiguous historical shared checks as individual acknowledgements. No elaborate active-check conversion or extra decision is required. If assessment unexpectedly finds an active list, stop/report rather than discard it.
5. If a disk reseed is necessary, compare disk/database by stable recipe ID and supported recipe facts before mutation. Alex reports no UI recipe edits and Dreaming synchronization. Verify that expected matching state; stop/report unexpected content or membership mismatches rather than pick a winner. No per-recipe UI-edit conflict-resolution workflow is required solely for hypothetical edits. Preserve household data/IDs, revision safeguards against actual concurrency and input copies.

## Remaining engineering and release gates

Dataset adoption still requires pinned licence text/version/hash, EN/FR exact-match/purchase corpus and governance review. CNF remains a pilot recommendation, not automatic adoption. Public schema/API/client/mock, real PostgreSQL/files/browser and current-format recovery acceptance remain required during separately approved implementation. Conditional fallback is not the default and cannot proceed past an unexpected mismatch without further assessment. The five newly settled product decisions are no longer approval holds.

## Future CI and default-selection requirements

Source observation includes concurrent parity changes, not just committed HEAD: `pwa/package.json:test:e2e:ci` now points at `production-browser.cjs`; `e2e-suites.cjs` now defines all as the four mocked suites and dynamically lists `*-live`. These edits are owned by `restore-local-ci-browser-parity` and are not yet independent verified defaults. Do not copy their implementation or restore old behavior. Parent research about d51222f is historical input where live work differs.

Future apply must:

- Use the parity owner's qualified production build/start path, owned resources and same effective configuration. `task test:e2e:ci -- <spec> --workers=4 --retries=0` is the current proposed focused path; confirm final parity semantics before execution. Development server, inherited BASE_URL or external image does not establish production artifact identity.
- Explicitly cover planning (groceries, servings, prepared and movement), recipes (editor, original/preview/quiet layout), tonight (Home/Cook and instruction recovery), and household (capture/report/recovery) where the slice crosses them. Final mocked qualification uses the four named suites via `task check:push:pwa SUITES='tonight planning recipes household'`; all must mean that exact mocked inventory, never silently include live suites. New browser files must be assigned to their capability inventory during their own future apply.
- Retain static contract + generated-client + stateful method-sensitive mock checks. Every changed DTO/status/SSE transition must agree across GET/PATCH/refresh/late replies. Mock browser passes do not prove PostgreSQL publication or migration.
- Require real isolated PostgreSQL via `task test:database -- --filter ...` for concurrency, guarded content, conversion/resume, report-triggered publication and recovery. Ordinary `task test:api` can skip opt-in PostgreSQL tests. Attribute/environment and actual selected/started/completed counts must demonstrate zero skips for required cases; --passWithNoTests and an empty filter are not evidence.
- Qualify selected real browser/API/DB cases explicitly with the existing `WFS_CALENDAR_LIVE=1` route and owned isolated resources after reviewing harness prerequisites. Merely inventorying a new `*-live.spec.ts` or passing mocked defaults does not run it. Add opt-in migration/recovery seams without enabling real providers or production services. A failure to provision is blocked, never skipped-as-pass.
- Keep deterministic fixed clock/deployment timezone, provider fixtures only at external boundaries, no real AI/translation calls, no production household services. Recompute must assert zero provider calls.
- Report first-attempt pass, retry pass, final failure, skipped, blocked and never-run stages separately. Store source/build/config/tool/platform and exact selected-case identity; hosted CI on the final candidate is distinct from native Mac validation. No cache or earlier waiver can stand in for new contract seams.

This planning session only runs document/OpenSpec checks with explicit paths, avoiding shared browser ports, builds, database containers and concurrent app tests. Future broader CI/default changes need their own authorized tooling scope after parity results settle.

## Recommended review and release sequence

The approved all-spec implementation now extracts the smallest coherent canonical
saved-row identity/guarded-publication prerequisite before grocery closure; see the
[extraction review](grocery-prerequisite-review.md). Legacy observed recipe/name
membership cannot prove positive incompatible-unit continuation. Grocery remains
open during this prerequisite, including exact recovery/client qualification before
canonical write activation. This dependency extraction does not complete the
canonical or migration companions or narrow any accepted grocery behavior.

After the prerequisite, complete grocery acceptance, then remaining canonical
facts/guarded capture, bilingual saved identity and mandatory step uses in dependency
order (the latter two can be independent after the foundation). Rehearse complete
in-place migration, client fencing and current-format recovery before activation.
Release the full portions outcome only after step scaling, current prepared reading
and required integration/visual corpus pass. Production cutover is a separate
operator approval with exact candidate and verified recovery packet.
# Bilingual shopping identity

## Why

Mechanical description normalization cannot safely identify equivalent French/English foods or distinguish preparation from purchase facts. Grocery generation must use saved validated identities deterministically.

## Outcome and Scope

App-owned IDs, validated EN/FR labels and exact aliases, protected shopping names and import/reprocessing proposals. No runtime AI, automatic dictionary-wide publication or translation-based guesses. Dataset choice remains gated by corpus/licence evaluation.

## What Changes

- **BREAKING:** adopt the applicable shared [contract](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) with explicit compatibility/failure behavior.
- Preserve user decisions and existing safety boundaries in the shared [review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md).
- Add adversarial acceptance from the shared [corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md); no product implementation in this session.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `grocery-shopping`: apply this change’s bounded grocery requirements.

## Impact

Depends on the canonical foundation and companion ownership map as specified in design.md. Future apply must synchronize OpenAPI, generated clients, consumers and stateful mocks where affected, and qualify actual persistence/workflow seams. Planning existence does not establish implementation readiness.
# Canonical recipe facts and original-basis correction

## Why

String edits and retained `RawMetadata.supply` currently have different owners; one changed string can invalidate the measured collection. Portions, cooking and groceries need the same exact saved facts and safe correction boundary.

## Outcome and Scope

Evolve this existing foundation, rather than replace it. One original-basis recipe content revision owns ordered ingredient rows, steps and their associations. Amount/unit remain independently nullable; exact fractions and ranges survive. The ordinary three-field editor stays quiet. Alex has approved absolute-allocation preservation, range comparison and new split/merge row behavior. Dataset and contract qualification remain engineering gates; artifact existence is not implementation approval or readiness.

## What Changes

- **BREAKING:** lossless scalar/range quantities, stable line/step IDs and `contentRevision` replace the proposed scalar-only, ingredient-only revision contract.
- Save original facts from every context; preserve human edits, explicit clearing, retained sources and existing serving protections.
- **BREAKING:** guarded atomic writes for ingredients, basis, instructions and shopping corrections; reject unversioned old editors before any field changes.
- Capture/import/reprocessing publish through the same guarded owner; preserve existing user reporting and eligible repair triggers. No selective candidate endpoint or dashboard.
- Share one server projection across Home, detail, Cook and grocery demand. Mandatory step scaling is owned by the companion below, not omitted from the release.
- Split the earlier cooking, grocery and recovery deltas into their companion owners; no main capability sync or archive in this session.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `recipe-ingredients`: canonical original facts, exact quantities, identity and publication.

### Modified Capabilities

- `recipe-editing`: original-basis drafts and coherent guarded Save.
- `recipe-library`: original canonical DTO and independent nullable basis.
- `recipe-capture`: coherent new capture and protected reprocessing publication.
- `recipe-sharing`: lower-fidelity text sharing remains distinct from backups.
- `supper-servings`: canonical original facts feed the existing shared projector.

## Impact

RecipeService, SupperIngredientProjection, import/synthesis/disk publication, generated client, editor, stateful mocks and PostgreSQL persistence will change only during a separately approved apply. Proposed shapes live in [contracts.md](contracts.md); the shared [review](review.md) and [acceptance corpus](acceptance-corpus.md) govern five bounded units. Companions: [groceries](../restore-dependable-grocery-interactions/proposal.md), [bilingual identity](../bilingual-shopping-identity/proposal.md), [steps](../scale-cooking-step-ingredients/proposal.md), [migration/recovery](../migrate-canonical-recipe-model/proposal.md).


## Fresh canonical web intake — separate publication review

The ordinary editor is now composed and qualified for explicitly converted recipes. The next bounded publication milestone is the existing fresh URL-import workflow producing editable canonical facts before readiness. It uses the current publication journal, workflow launch evidence and current recipe codec; no separate converter service, recovery endpoint or provider is introduced.

Alex approved retaining usable wording when a provably fresh import cannot safely represent trustworthy canonical facts. Publish that wording into the existing unready editable review path with a distinct retained-material receipt, preserve source and the existing failure/retry path, and flag it for review. Do not mark this as a completed extraction or ready recipe. The normal lossless path publishes exact canonical facts atomically. Honest absent measurements remain valid. A changed eligible comment on this witnessed review material can launch a narrowly guarded repair that selects captured human corrections and validates lossless canonical facts before readiness. Other existing-recipe reimport/repair remains fenced until its saved-identity/protection merge is qualified.

This milestone does not create validated ingredient-use bindings. Conversion currently creates empty bindings, ordinary step edits only carry prior ones, and projection deliberately never discovers them. Original step wording stays readable under the existing quiet-uncertainty rule. The ordinary binding-proposal/semantic-validation inlet remains a necessary separate step-companion dependency before claiming the complete whole-use portions tracer.

## Approved next slice: correct flagged recipes in the existing editor

Alex approved preserving manual ingredient and step editing for incomplete imports and clarified that the existing report flag must be used, not a new draft product concept. Qualifying retained content needing correction is accessible through the existing Ready for review queue and issue badge; Reported remains its existing superset. The existing detail editor edits saved original ingredients and original steps, including an intentional original-content entry when a dated projection is unavailable. Blank amount/unit and unbound instruction text remain valid. Late automation cannot overwrite human corrections; invalidated scaling proof stops applying without hiding the text or adding a persistent notice. This correction slice does not authorize the separate fresh-source publication cutover, semantic binding production or catalogue adoption.

## Reviewed system-review refinement (2026-11-10)

Alex approved a system flag only for actual ingredient/usable-step validation needs on retained editable recipe content. Use the existing Ready for review status and generic explanation, with a short system-authored explanatory comment and no repair launch. Unchanged feedback Save is a no-op; a changed human comment keeps the existing eligible correction rules (source URL/images, Ingredients/Steps, no Duplicate), history and stale-write protection. Do not turn image/category/transport failures into content reports or overwrite existing feedback. This is a limited bridge from content validation to the existing review queue, not replacement of failed-capture management. Review wording must not claim a re-import happened. Resolve retains its existing feedback-only semantics.

Use the existing Clear/deferred-cleanup guard conservatively: persisted ingredient/instruction/canonical content, including explicit empty saved collections, survives. This also retains some partial automated content; the trade-off avoids a new human-ownership marker/schema or recovery mechanism. Empty placeholders remain eligible for existing cleanup. Preserve the original-step editor and original-content entry, and verify system review → manual correction → reopen → changed comment correction, no-op unchanged save (including after backup/read-back), report preservation, clear protection and stale-job safety. The earlier broad failure-flag proposal is superseded; fresh canonical source publication and binding production remain separate, unimplemented scope. Broader tasks and archive stay open until required acceptance passes.
# Migrate and recover canonical recipe content

## Why

The complete model must survive upgrade and recovery without losing household links or human edits. Dreaming and management already share disk backup, seed and sync owners; those owners must retain canonical facts rather than exporting and restoring legacy-only fields.

## Outcome and Scope

In-place-first conversion, conditional recipe-only disk fallback, current-format-only recovery, staged client fencing and fresh-list upgrade without historical deletion. No default reseed, production operation, old backup compatibility, automatic extraction or silent disk-over-live precedence. Conditional fallback compares stable IDs and stops/reports unexpected mismatches.

## What Changes

- **BREAKING:** adopt the applicable shared [contract](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) with explicit compatibility/failure behavior.
- Preserve user decisions and existing safety boundaries in the shared [review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md).
- Evolve Dreaming → db-backup → BackupDatabase → `ManagementService.BackupAsync` (also management backup POST), management seed → `RestoreAsync`, and guarded recipe sync/publication. Reuse the current recipe codec; do not add a parallel recovery API or user-facing package workflow.
- Keep recipe-only forward reprocessing separate from household seed. Whole-installation database-and-asset backup remains separate disk-loss and rollback protection.
- Qualify edit → existing backup → seed into an independent disposable destination → compare → repeat, including exact canonical facts, retained media and protected household/history/extras.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `data-backup-and-recovery`: forward migration and complete current-format recovery.
- `grocery-shopping`: apply this change’s bounded grocery requirements.

## Impact

Depends on the canonical foundation and companion ownership map as specified in design.md. Any public contract change must synchronize OpenAPI, generated clients, consumers and stateful mocks; this bounded existing-operation slice changes no public operation or DTO. Qualify actual persistence/workflow seams. Planning existence does not establish implementation readiness.
> **Superseded, unimplemented — 2026-11-07.** Do not apply this separate ingredient-candidate proposal. Its tasks remain unchecked as historical planning. Use canonical guarded import/reprocessing plus manual correction. Existing user recipe flags, Report/Review issue and eligible repair triggers remain supported, including their safety and retry safeguards. See [replacement foundation](../canonical-ingredient-correction/proposal.md). No archive or main-spec sync has occurred.

# Proposal — selective ingredient repair (deferred)

## Why
After safe conversion and manual correction exist, some evidenced missing or conflicting facts may still require consulting retained original sources. The current full re-import graph can overwrite unrelated content and media, so it is unsuitable for ingredient-only assistance.

## Outcome and Scope
Stage 3 is a deferred option dependent on `canonical-ingredient-correction`, to activate only if remaining manual correction effort justifies it. No stage 1 or 2 task depends on this change. Prepare the bounded candidate workflow; do not execute it through this planning approval.

## What Changes
- Explicitly select evidenced gaps and usable retained sources; skip accepted facts and valid unquantified content. No automatic repair on read, migration or API startup.
- Generate ingredient-only candidates using existing source loaders/provider boundary/workflow infrastructure, without publishing live facts, files, hero, basis or instructions.
- Validate evidence, identities and captured ingredient/basis/source revisions; treat provider confidence as insufficient evidence.
- Offer selected corrections inside existing Edit, publishing only through explicit revision-guarded Save. Keep Search flags separate from household reports.
- Retain resumable work outcomes and recoverable candidate/source relationships; restored candidates require revalidation and never trigger provider work automatically.

## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
- `ingredient-repair`: selective source-assisted candidates, validation, acceptance and recovery.

### Modified Capabilities
None. This capability extends the stage 2 guarded publication/recovery boundaries without replacing their contracts.

## Impact
An additive repair request/candidate contract, regenerated client and method-sensitive mocks, existing workflows/source loaders, recipe editor and full-fidelity recovery coverage. No new provider platform, review dashboard, automatic batch correction, full-share format or legacy storage deletion.

See [stage boundaries](../archive/2026-11-06-quiet-recipe-portions/scope-stages.md). All tasks remain unchecked and explicitly deferred; implementation requires a separate selected-stage request. DV reset and production actions remain separate.

# Design

## Context and Existing Ownership

`IngredientNormalizer`, `UnitNormalizer`, `AisleMapper`, `CategorizeIngredientsProcessor` and `GroceryRecomputeService` currently use normalized raw supply names. Canonical publication replaces stale evidence reads; identity mapping is saved at import/correction, never guessed per grocery refresh. See [dataset evaluation](sources.md).

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

App-owned IDs outlive upstream code changes. Confirmed preparation variants can share an ID; purchase qualifiers keep fresh/canned, salted/unsalted, dietary and product forms separate. A food ID is not a row ID: grams and volume may remain separate shopping rows. Missing translation keeps source shopping spelling and deterministic fallback key. Do not publish unvalidated EN/FR labels as facts or strip accents blindly when they create collisions.

A curated initial vocabulary and safe fallback is preferable to a large permissive-but-noisy automatic crosswalk. # Design

## Context and Existing Ownership

Current `ManagementService`, `RecipeExportContent`, `SyncRecipeProcessor`, `RecipeRepository` and online recovery owners span database, disk/media and durable workflows. Existing ordinary restore supports legacy arrays and missing artifacts; several main requirements must change together. Recipe-only fallback must not invoke general seed/disaster recovery unchanged because those owners also mutate household data.

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

Default in-place preserves live recipes and stable IDs. Capture source/current facts and protected hashes, convert only proven associations with one owner per recipe and publish atomically guarded. Ambiguous trusted measurements that cannot be represented safely keep legacy read access until manual reconciliation; do not erase them for a migration completion percentage.

Current-format ordinary merge and explicitly selected exact replacement are separate. Version and timestamps cannot establish precedence. An old backup is unsupported, not implicitly convertible inside restore. The one-time forward importer accepts only its manifest's input list; legacy source readability during this process does not promise continued old-backup support. Existing historical voter privacy, extras, report state and preparation/serving recovery remain intact.

## Existing operations own canonical backup and seed

Dreaming’s db-backup step invokes BackupDatabase and the same `ManagementService.BackupAsync` as POST `/api/management/backup`. POST `/api/management/seed` invokes `RestoreAsync`; evolve these owners to write/read the existing version-2 canonical recipe codec. Keep the existing disk layout and management routes. Any necessary format/integrity inventory is internal to these operations, not a second recovery API or user-facing package. Whole-installation database plus asset backup remains a separate protection against disk loss and migration rollback.

Preflight canonical input before household mutation. New destination recipes retain exported IDs and exact canonical content; repeated identical seed is idempotent. A divergent current destination is not authority to overwrite newer human facts: preserve it and report conflict unless the existing captured revision/publication owner proves authority. Sync remains recipe-only and uses captured input, revision guards and durable publication/retry ownership; it must never invoke household seed or infer permission from timestamps. Legacy readability before activation is not a promise of permanent old-backup support; cutover remains fenced until the current-only boundary is qualified.

## First Observable Slice

Disposable PostgreSQL plus copied recipe/media store → no-write manifest → convert one 4-portion 1/3-cup recipe with current edits and one partial step → existing Dreaming/management backup → management seed into an isolated destination → independent read-back → repeat. Compare every canonical field, source/media hash, relationship and protected household field; distinguish this seed merge from independent whole-installation exact restore; interrupt before/after commit and resume idempotently. Prove unsupported old format preflight has zero writes before widening batches.

## Compatibility, Rollout and Reversal

Use [rollout](../canonical-ingredient-correction/rollout.md). All old writers, workers, background sync and tabs must be fenced. Export unsaved drafts locally through the supported upgrade route before refresh; old full editor payloads with ingredients cannot masquerade as unrelated updates. Prepared counts, dates, history, family members, votes, assignments, human rotation/discoverability and grocery-extra lineages are protected.

Alex confirms there will be no active grocery list during update; the next recipe-derived list is new. Do not migrate old name-level checks or infer individual row intent. New recipe rows start unchecked without demand baselines. Preserve historical lists/check maps and extra occurrences/history, with extras retaining their existing lifecycle. No active-check conversion decision or special shopping acknowledgement UI is needed. Unexpected active-list evidence stops assessment for reporting, not automatic deletion.

A verified independent pre-cutover snapshot plus exact old executable/schema is the emergency rollback pair. After new writes, simply rolling back an image is unsafe; choose compatible full-state recovery or forward fix. Fresh current-format backup after conversion is separately read back and verified before routine operations resume; it cannot protect the migration interval retroactively.

## Conditional Disk Fallback

Only if in-place assessment establishes a concrete unresolvable blocker, prepare recipe-only fallback. Inventory both disk/live versions, IDs, source/media and field ownership; preserve input copies independently. No delete-all, auto-created missing IDs, soft-delete resurrection or purging database-only recipes. Household state, notes/rating/manual flags, attribution, creation/deletion, occurrences and relationship IDs stay untouched. Stage selected recipe fields only; revision-guard publication and durable derived rebuild. Record converted/deferred entries and resume input/output identities. For fallback, compare disk and database by stable recipe ID before publication; report unexpected content or membership mismatches and stop rather than choosing a winner.

Alex reports no recipe edits through the UI and says Dreaming has kept disk and database in sync. Treat matching recipe IDs/content as the expected case and verify it, allowing only documented representation differences from conversion. If an ID is missing on either side or supported recipe facts unexpectedly differ, stop/report the fallback before mutation rather than silently replacing content. No elaborate per-recipe edit-conflict workflow or general disk/live precedence selector is required solely for hypothetical UI edits. Keep revision guards against actual concurrent changes, input preservation and household protections. A timestamp is not evidence of equality. Do not overwrite source files before independent preservation and validation.

## Operational Diagnosis

Separate conversion status, committed facts, pending derived rebuild and completed verification. Record no sensitive raw recipe/provider payload in routine logs. A failure preserves prior usable content; a conflict is neither empty success nor forced replacement. Test current-format merge stale/divergent content, identical revision with different bytes, crash/restart, stale work, mixed old clients and media publication gaps before release.

See the shared [dependency/conflict review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md) for approval and release order, and [acceptance corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md) for preservation cases. Proposed API/schema details have one owner in [contracts.md](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md).

This document is the sole shape proposal for all five changes. `specs/openapi.yaml` remains runtime contract authority and is untouched in this spec-only session. Names below are proposed additions, not claims about current endpoints. Dependent tasks must first approve and transcribe them to OpenAPI, regenerate Kiota and synchronize method-sensitive mocks. ## Recipe content and exact quantities

```json
{
  "contentSchemaVersion": 2,
  "contentRevision": "opaque-token",
  "servings": 4,
  "ingredientLines": [{
    "id": "uuid",
    "description": "pasta",
    "amount": {"kind":"scalar", "value":{"n":"200","d":"1"}},
    "amountText": "200",
    "unit": {"text":"g", "definitionId":"mass:g"},
    "scaling": "proportional",
    "package": null,
    "shopping": {"name":"pasta", "foodId":null, "mappingRevision":null},
    "provenance": {"origin":"human", "sourceRef":null, "protectedFields":["amount"]}
  }],
  "instructionSections": [{"id":"uuid", "name":null, "steps":[{
    "id":"uuid", "text":"Add 200 g pasta.", "textRevision":"opaque-step-token", "bindings":[]
  }]}]
}
```

IDs are server-issued UUIDs; create drafts carry a request-local clientId mapped in the authoritative result, not a claimed saved ID. Lists define order. Sections preserve supported nested source ordering without a general nested recipe engine. A step's textRevision changes only with its text; contentRevision changes on semantic content publication. Source metadata has sourceRevision plus content-addressed evidence references. Keep evidence access behind existing household authorization; shared DTOs need not expose raw private evidence.

`amount` is null, scalar as above, or `{"kind":"range","min":{"n":"2","d":"1"},"max":{"n":"3","d":"1"}}`. Nonnegative normalized numerator strings and positive denominator strings have at most 38 decimal digits each, no leading zeros except zero, gcd=1; endpoints ordered min≤max. Transport uses strings to avoid JS safe-integer loss. Arithmetic uses checked exact intermediates; overflow returns unresolved projection with original evidence, never saturation/NaN. API rejects invalid persisted values with 400. `amountText` retains supported original spelling (including Unicode fractions) only if it parses to the identical amount; generated projections never replace it. Null amount requires null amountText; unparsed imported text remains description/evidence, not a numeric assertion.

Input grammar in the amount field: unsigned integer, dot decimal or locale French comma decimal (no thousands separators), ASCII proper/improper fraction n/d, mixed whole + fraction, listed Unicode fractions ¼ ½ ¾ ⅐ ⅑ ⅒ ⅓ ⅔ ⅕ ⅖ ⅗ ⅘ ⅙ ⅚ ⅛ ⅜ ⅝ ⅞, or two such scalars separated by hyphen/en dash. Normalize spaces, reject exponent, negative sign, denominator zero, multiple separators and ambiguous `1,000` (offer correction, never infer 1000). Range input is explicit; do not parse a hyphen in arbitrary ingredient prose. Original notation survives a round trip; output formatting uses deterministic locale conventions without feeding rounded values back to storage.

Unit is independently null, or `{text, definitionId:null|supported-id}`. Null unit is no declared unit, not an assertion of pieces. Unitless known counts can group together; do not merge them with cloves/cans absent explicit count semantics. Supported exact definitions start with metric mass/volume and explicit count kinds. Alex approved preserving cups, teaspoons and tablespoons in three independent unit families, with equivalent English/French aliases normalized within each family (cup/cups/tasse/tasses; tsp/teaspoon/c. à thé; tbsp/tablespoon/c. à soupe). Quantities remain in their declared family without automatic conversion to millilitres or between culinary families. Existing implicit 240/15/5 ml assumptions are not the desired behavior and cannot populate new definition IDs. Regional definitions must be explicit and validated. No mass/volume or drained/net conversion without evidence. `package` is null or `{countUnit, capacity:{amount,unit}, basis:"net"|"drained"|"unspecified"}`; capacity stays fixed while the line's count scales. No purchase rounding.

not a recovered original fraction. If only a finite nonnegative double remains,
interpret its invariant shortest round-trip decimal as a bounded compatibility

that evidence distinction internally. Apply the same 38-digit normalized rational

# Recipe ingredient contract delta

## Purpose

Own ordered original ingredient facts and their safe publication so recipe editing, reading, cooking and grocery derivation use the same saved measurements.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Own current ingredient facts in one ordered collection
A recipe SHALL expose one versioned current ingredient collection with stable line identity/order, free-text description, nullable exact scalar-or-range amount and independently nullable unit. Its compatible strings and context-specific projections SHALL derive from those same facts. Retained extraction metadata SHALL remain evidence rather than an independent current writer. Serving basis SHALL remain independently nullable.

#### Scenario: Shared facts across contexts
- **WHEN** original, preview and captured dated consumers read a saved recipe
- **THEN** they use the same line identities, descriptions and original amounts with their existing context-specific target rules
- **AND** grocery derivation scales those unrounded original facts before grouping and conversion

#### Scenario: Metadata differs after a correction
- **WHEN** saved canonical facts differ from retained extraction supply
- **THEN** current reads use saved canonical facts and retain the extraction evidence without replaying it over the correction

### Requirement: Permit independently optional quantity fields
An ingredient SHALL allow amount and unit to be independently null. A nonempty row SHALL have a nonblank free-text description. Supplied scalar amounts and range endpoints SHALL be exact, bounded and nonnegative; zero and unitless counts SHALL remain valid. Missing amount or unit alone SHALL NOT make an ingredient invalid, require a special phrase or create household report membership.

#### Scenario: Every optional-field combination
- **WHEN** rows contain 2 with no unit, g with no amount, neither amount nor unit, or both 200 and g, each with a description
- **THEN** Save and reopen preserve each supplied or absent value independently without inventing a number or unit

#### Scenario: Qualitative ingredients
- **WHEN** a row describes salt to taste, oil for frying or another legitimately unquantified ingredient
- **THEN** it remains valid without requiring a recognized keyword or an extra quantity-state field

#### Scenario: Invalid supplied amount
- **WHEN** a supplied amount is negative, non-finite or nonnumeric
- **THEN** validation rejects that input without publishing any part of the ingredient mutation

### Requirement: Preserve human facts and extraction evidence
Canonical publication SHALL preserve current manual descriptions, quantities and explicit null choices against stale extraction, reimport and conversion work. Unknown legacy authorship SHALL NOT be assumed machine-owned. Retained raw extraction content SHALL remain available as evidence, including original numeric and serving-yield evidence.

#### Scenario: Automatic work finishes after manual Save
- **WHEN** conversion or extraction work captured an older content revision before a person saved a correction or cleared an amount
- **THEN** it cannot overwrite those saved facts and the original evidence remains retained

#### Scenario: Existing edited text disagrees with extraction
- **WHEN** legacy current text differs from retained extracted strings
- **THEN** conversion preserves current text and does not transfer measurements from the obsolete extraction by position

### Requirement: Convert trustworthy original facts conservatively
Supported legacy adapters SHALL preserve current wording/order and only unambiguously associated original measurements. They SHALL NOT infer quantities from arbitrary prose, scaled displays, positional supply matching or guessed serving basis. Conversion SHALL preserve reliable numeric amounts even with an unknown basis. A safe representation SHALL retain preparation/package wording and avoid duplicated quantity text.

#### Scenario: Known original amount with unknown basis
- **WHEN** coherent original evidence associates 200 g with pasta but serving basis is null
- **THEN** supported conversion retains 200 g and null basis rather than losing the amount or treating a dated display as its source

#### Scenario: Untrusted or ambiguous association
- **WHEN** legacy rows are duplicated, reordered or changed so a supply association is not provable
- **THEN** their current descriptions/order and evidence remain retained without guessed numeric transfers

#### Scenario: Trusted facts cannot be represented safely
- **WHEN** an adapter cannot preserve both a trustworthy original measurement and current wording without duplication or rewriting
- **THEN** canonical conversion is deferred for that recipe with an explicit conflict outcome and the legacy read adapter remains available until explicit reconciliation

### Requirement: Guard resumable canonical publication
Per-recipe conversion and canonical publication SHALL compare the captured content revision before atomically publishing. Successful unchanged retries SHALL be idempotent. Before conversion the supported legacy read adapter owns current reads; after conversion canonical facts alone own them. Explicit empty collections and null facts SHALL not revive legacy values.

#### Scenario: Recipe changes during conversion
- **WHEN** a person changes ingredients after conversion inspection but before publication
- **THEN** the stale conversion does not overwrite the newer recipe and reports a conflict for reconciliation

#### Scenario: Retry a completed conversion
- **WHEN** an unchanged successfully converted recipe is processed again
- **THEN** its identities, facts and human protection remain equivalent without duplicate rows or a new correction

#### Scenario: Explicitly cleared collection
- **WHEN** a person saves an empty canonical collection while retained metadata still contains supplies
- **THEN** subsequent original, dated, grocery and recovery reads do not revive those old supplies

### Requirement: Require coherent recovery before write cutover

Canonical writes SHALL activate only with verified current-format recovery of exact quantities, identities, revisions, source evidence, human protection and independent serving basis. Ordinary text sharing SHALL NOT claim this fidelity.

#### Scenario: Recovery owner gate
- **WHEN** canonical write activation is proposed
- **THEN** the migration/recovery companion must have passed its current-format round-trip and staged client gates; old backup decoding is not a prerequisite

### Requirement: Round trip exact original fractions and ranges

Canonical quantities SHALL preserve supported fraction/decimal notation and exact scalar or ordered closed-range values. Projections SHALL always start from original facts, scale both endpoints and retain fixed package capacities. Invalid or out-of-bounds input SHALL fail without partial publication.

#### Scenario: Fraction without drift
- **WHEN** original 1/3 cup for three is previewed for five then three
- **THEN** storage and the returned original remain exactly 1/3 cup

#### Scenario: Range and packages
- **WHEN** 2–3 cloves and two 400 g cans for four are read for eight
- **THEN** they project 4–6 cloves and four 400 g cans, with no purchase rounding

#### Scenario: Unknown and invalid are different
- **WHEN** amount is absent, zero, an inverted range or a fraction with zero denominator
- **THEN** absence stays unknown, zero stays valid, and the invalid supplied forms reject without saving other fields

### Requirement: Own stable original steps under the same content revision

Canonical content SHALL retain ordered stable ingredient, section and step IDs with original editable step text. Ingredients, basis, steps, validated use associations and saved shopping corrections SHALL share one content revision. Retained raw metadata SHALL NOT independently overwrite these current facts.

#### Scenario: Reorder and rename
- **WHEN** a person reorders rows or changes one description
- **THEN** retained row IDs do not change and step references do not shift by index

#### Scenario: One coherent revision
- **WHEN** content is read during a concurrent ingredient and step save
- **THEN** a projection contains one committed content revision, never ingredients from one and step bindings from another
## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Display returned ingredient strings in detail

Original reading SHALL show rendered canonical current descriptions and optional quantities in order, including its compatible returned string projection, with no invented rows when absent. Dated/preview reading SHALL use the shared projection of those same line identities with original access. Reads SHALL NOT change stored ingredients; legacy parsing belongs to the supported boundary adapter, not independent screen logic.

#### Scenario: Read returned ingredients
- **WHEN** original detail returns Pasta followed by Sauce
- **THEN** Ingredients lists Pasta followed by Sauce

#### Scenario: No ingredients are returned
- **WHEN** successful detail has no ingredient strings
- **THEN** Ingredients remains present without invented rows

#### Scenario: Home and its dated cooking view
- **WHEN** Home Tonight and Cook are opened for the same captured planned occurrence
- **THEN** their ingredient facts and target count agree rather than one independently showing raw unscaled strings
- **AND** explicit original review and undated Quick Find retain original context from the same current ingredient owner

### Requirement: Return persisted servings in the recipe DTO

Public recipe reads SHALL expose the saved nullable integer servings plus canonical original description/amount/unit rows and content revision through their documented response contract; compatible ingredients strings are derived. Unknown count remains null. Existing envelopes/access/eligibility apply, and reads SHALL NOT call AI or mutate ingredient storage.

#### Scenario: Known count in detail
- **WHEN** authorized GET /api/recipes/{id} retrieves a recipe with stored servings 4
- **THEN** HTTP 200 includes recipe.servings equal to 4 in its existing unwrapped recipe/updatedAt response

#### Scenario: Unknown count
- **WHEN** a successful recipe DTO read retrieves a recipe with null servings
- **THEN** its servings is null without defaulting to 2 or 4

### Requirement: Correct or add servings through recipe editing

Authorized recipe editing SHALL correct/add a positive whole basis within database integer range using the captured content revision and existing Save/Cancel recovery. Saving preserves raw yield and original ingredient quantities and adds no basis/count field to recipe.info. Omitted count preserves its current value, including null. Stale/unversioned basis writes at canonical cutover SHALL conflict without partial updates.

#### Scenario: Correct a known count
- **WHEN** a user changes servings from 4 to 3 and successfully saves the recipe
- **THEN** subsequent detail reads and reopening show 3, even if raw recipeYield still says “4 portions”, with original ingredient quantities and raw metadata retained

#### Scenario: Add a missing count
- **WHEN** a user edits a recipe with null servings, enters 2 and successfully saves
- **THEN** subsequent detail reads show 2 and the viewing heading shows the localized two-serving badge

#### Scenario: Omitted count preserves stored state
- **WHEN** a recipe update omits servings, including an older client's request or an untouched blank field for an unknown count
- **THEN** the existing count or null remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Invalid count
- **WHEN** a user supplies zero, a negative, fractional, out-of-range or nonnumeric count
- **THEN** editing presents an associated localized validation error and prevents saving that input, and direct API requests with invalid supplied counts are rejected without changing the recipe

#### Scenario: Cancel or failed save
- **WHEN** the user cancels a changed servings draft or saving fails
- **THEN** Cancel discards the draft, while failure retains it for correction or retry and does not present the new count as successfully saved

#### Scenario: Preserve a newer basis or ingredient edit
- **WHEN** the loaded content revision is stale or required revision is absent when basis is submitted
- **THEN** the server rejects the update as a refresh/conflict, preserves current state and the client retains the draft rather than declaring success
## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Share one authoritative projection across consumers

Home dated ingredients, proposed/assigned detail, cooking and groceries SHALL share canonical original facts and server-owned dated scaling. Temporary previews use that owner with an independent count. Assigned reads reject stale occurrence identity; original reads remain compatible through the common adapter. Reads SHALL NOT assign, save portions, call providers or materialize preparation.

#### Scenario: Plan and cook for six
- **WHEN** a recipe with basis two and 200 g pasta is planned for six
- **THEN** dated detail and cooking show 600 g and its grocery contribution is 600 g

#### Scenario: Proposed date before assignment
- **WHEN** an unassigned candidate is read for a date configured for four
- **THEN** its default dated projection uses four without requiring assignment or changing saved state

#### Scenario: No selected or proposed date
- **WHEN** recipe reading has no date context
- **THEN** its default is original quantities and an explicitly selected 2/4/6 preview remains a separate read-only projection

#### Scenario: Converted and edited canonical record
- **WHEN** a canonical content revision replaces legacy live supply reads
- **THEN** all quantity consumers use that revision and its original amounts, with grocery normalization/aggregation after projection rather than another recipe ingredient parser

#### Scenario: Home ingredients and dated Cook agree
- **WHEN** Home Tonight and Cook refer to the same captured assigned recipe, date and effective portions
- **THEN** Home uses the shared dated projection with the same reliable amounts and completeness before display rounding, including frozen prepared portions
- **AND** late results from an earlier recipe/date/occurrence cannot replace the current list; pending, failure or changed-plan state is explicit rather than labeling original strings as scaled
- **AND** opening the ingredient list performs no assignment, portions, grocery, preparation or completion write

### Requirement: Scale independently aligned ingredient amounts

Known canonical amounts SHALL scale only for their stable original-basis line identities. Missing/uncertain lines do not invalidate other known lines. Legacy name/source matching is a conservative conversion/import boundary, not a second live quantity owner. Unknown/conflicting facts retain text. Reads SHALL NOT guess text numbers, call AI or repair saved data.

#### Scenario: Four-portion shells recipe with omitted seasonings
- **WHEN** original yield is four and canonical lines converted from coherent unambiguous source facts retain 12 shells, 1 onion, 450 g beef and 500 ml marinara while salt and pepper lack reliable amounts
- **THEN** preview two shows 6 shells, 0.5 onion, 225 g beef and 250 ml marinara; preview four shows 12, 1, 450 g and 500 ml; preview six shows 18, 1.5, 675 g and 750 ml
- **AND** seasonings retain their original text and honest completeness state, other verified lines scale, and the recipe is not described as completely quantified

#### Scenario: Missing middle ingredient
- **WHEN** a lime line has no structured amount between verified garlic and honey, followed by known salmon and sesame amounts
- **THEN** garlic, honey, salmon and sesame retain their own amounts and scale independently; lime is not given honey's quantity

#### Scenario: Ambiguous duplicate or changed source
- **WHEN** legacy conversion cannot associate an amount unambiguously, source/current strings conflict or an association has become invalid without an explicit accepted correction
- **THEN** affected amounts are unresolved instead of guessed, and unrelated verified bindings remain usable

#### Scenario: Intentional unquantified text and packages
- **WHEN** an ingredient says salt to taste or oil for frying, or a verified quantity is two 400 g cans
- **THEN** the direction remains ordinary unquantified text and scaling changes the can count without multiplying its package size or instruction numbers

#### Scenario: Shared consumers and unknown basis
- **WHEN** the same aligned recipe/count is read through preview, proposed or assigned detail, cooking and grocery contribution
- **THEN** reliable numeric amounts and completeness agree across consumers before display rounding
- **AND** an unknown original yield prevents a scaling factor, offers original evidence/correction, and is never replaced by family size

#### Scenario: Explicit canonical identities distinguish duplicate names
- **WHEN** distinct canonical lines have the same descriptive name but their own accepted amounts and stable identities
- **THEN** scaling retains each association without re-matching names or inventing identity from grocery grouping keys

#### Scenario: Valid unquantified lines and correction flags
- **WHEN** a canonical collection includes legitimate unquantified directions beside numeric amounts
- **THEN** the directions remain ordinary text without a correction flag solely for missing numbers; technical completeness and saved household report membership retain their separate meanings

# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Open initialized recipe-detail field drafts

For successfully loaded library detail, Settings SHALL offer Edit initialized from the authoritative saved detail: name, description, canonical ingredient rows, serving basis, cuisine and meal types. Ingredient drafts SHALL retain line identities and the captured content revision. Absent optional text and ingredients SHALL initialize empty; unknown basis SHALL remain unknown.

#### Scenario: Edit loaded detail
- **WHEN** a person opens Settings and activates Edit on successfully loaded library detail
- **THEN** the sheet offers initialized name, description, ingredient and cuisine fields, meal-type choices, Save changes and Cancel

#### Scenario: Initialize meal-type choices
- **WHEN** the person opens Edit
- **THEN** nonempty loaded meal types supply the draft choices
- **AND** if none are loaded, a trimmed category matching an offered choice supplies one choice, otherwise Supper supplies the draft default
- **AND** the offered choices are Breakfast, Brunch, Snack, Lunch, Supper, Sides, Dessert, Appetizer and Beverage

#### Scenario: Enter ordinary editing from Search
- **WHEN** a person opens an ordinary Search result and activates Edit
- **THEN** the existing editor initializes original saved ingredient facts and preserves its existing return navigation and household feedback semantics

### Requirement: Edit ingredient rows in the detail draft

The editor SHALL provide three separately labeled inputs per ingredient: amount, unit and free-text description. Amount and unit SHALL be independently optional, with no required quantity-state selector. It SHALL allow adding and removing rows. Changes SHALL affect only the draft before Save. Existing rows SHALL retain stable identities and relative order unless explicitly reordered; new rows SHALL receive new identities on save.

#### Scenario: Change and add ingredients
- **WHEN** a person changes an ingredient row and activates Add ingredient
- **THEN** the draft contains the changed row and an additional empty row

#### Scenario: Remove an ingredient
- **WHEN** a person removes a draft ingredient row
- **THEN** that row is removed while the other rows retain their relative order

#### Scenario: Correct a numeric amount or unit
- **WHEN** a person corrects an ingredient amount or unit in Edit
- **THEN** the draft permits the complete current description, amount and unit representation without silently retaining a conflicting old amount

#### Scenario: Independently blank quantity fields
- **WHEN** a person leaves amount blank, unit blank or both blank on a row with a description
- **THEN** the draft accepts those fields independently without requiring a confirmation choice or a recognized phrase

#### Scenario: Edit from a scaled view
- **WHEN** dated or preview reading shows 400 g for a recipe whose saved original line is 200 g pasta
- **THEN** Edit initializes amount 200, unit g and description pasta rather than 400
- **AND** an untouched measured row retains its own original facts when this row changes

### Requirement: Restrict local detail Save eligibility

The editor SHALL disable Save changes when the trimmed draft name is empty or no meal types are selected. Description, cuisine and ingredients SHALL be allowed to be empty in the local draft. Save SHALL also require valid supplied ingredient facts and a nonblank description on every nonempty row and a valid supplied positive serving basis; unknown omitted basis SHALL remain permitted.

#### Scenario: Name is blank
- **WHEN** the draft name is empty or whitespace-only
- **THEN** Save changes is disabled

#### Scenario: No meal type is selected
- **WHEN** the person deselects all draft meal types
- **THEN** Save changes is disabled until at least one is selected and the name is nonblank

#### Scenario: Reject invalid ingredient numeric input
- **WHEN** a supplied ingredient amount is negative, non-finite or nonnumeric
- **THEN** Save is unavailable with correction feedback in the editor and the draft is retained
- **AND** valid zero amounts, unitless counts and intentionally unquantified ingredients are not rejected solely for those forms

#### Scenario: Description required on a partial row
- **WHEN** a row contains an amount or unit but its description is blank
- **THEN** Save is disabled with row-associated feedback and the draft is retained rather than silently discarding that row

### Requirement: Submit normalized detail fields for the loaded recipe

Enabled Save SHALL PATCH the loaded recipe with normalized name, description, final ordered canonical ingredient lines, cuisine and meal types plus the captured content revision. Description/unit text SHALL be trimmed, blank optional amount/unit fields mapped independently to null and wholly blank ingredient rows removed in order; a row containing only amount or unit SHALL require a description rather than being silently dropped; blank cuisine SHALL remain null. A basis edit SHALL use the same revision. Canonical lines and legacy ingredient arrays SHALL NOT be submitted together.

#### Scenario: Submit edited fields
- **WHEN** enabled Save changes is activated for loaded recipe R
- **THEN** PATCH targets R with normalized name, description, ingredientLines, expectedContentRevision, cuisineType and mealTypes rather than a different recipe or only the changed field

#### Scenario: Submit blank optional drafts
- **WHEN** Save changes is activated with blank description, blank cuisine and only blank ingredient rows, with a valid name and meal selection
- **THEN** the submission contains description as an empty string, cuisineType as null and ingredientLines as an empty array

### Requirement: Apply supplied non-null recipe-detail update fields

Authorized PATCH SHALL retain existing top-level non-null/omission and empty-value semantics for detail fields. Within a supplied canonical row, explicit null amount or unit SHALL clear that optional fact; it SHALL NOT be interpreted as an omitted top-level field. Ingredient, basis, instruction and shopping-association mutations SHALL require the current content revision at write cutover; canonical lines SHALL replace the current ordered collection and derive legacy strings. Successful updates SHALL retain recipe identity and advance its timestamp. Other field-only requests SHALL remain compatible.

#### Scenario: Store supplied detail fields
- **WHEN** an authorized PATCH supplies valid non-null detail fields and a current revision for any ingredient, basis, instruction or shopping-association mutation for an existing recipe and the update succeeds
- **THEN** those values are stored for that ID and its update timestamp is assigned

#### Scenario: Preserve omitted or null values
- **WHEN** an authorized PATCH omits a detail field or supplies null and the update succeeds
- **THEN** that stored field is unchanged, including an existing cuisine receiving null

#### Scenario: Replace with empty values
- **WHEN** an authorized PATCH supplies an empty description, an empty cuisine string, empty canonical ingredients or empty meal types with the required current content revision and succeeds
- **THEN** each supplied empty value replaces its stored value
- **AND** supplying empty meal types sets category to Supper without adding Supper to the stored meal-type array

### Requirement: Display the submitted snapshot after successful detail Save

After successful detail Save, the client SHALL display the authoritative returned saved recipe, its content revision and saved original ingredient facts, then leave editing. It SHALL NOT reconstruct quantities from submitted strings alone. Unrelated saved facts and existing departure behavior SHALL remain governed by their owners.

#### Scenario: Save resolves successfully
- **WHEN** a submitted detail-field update resolves successfully while the sheet remains mounted
- **THEN** the sheet displays returned authoritative name, description, canonical ingredients, cuisine, meal types, content revision and original facts through its existing detail presentation and exits editing

### Requirement: Mark search-derived recipe state pending with supported updates

When an authorized recipe PATCH supplies a non-null supported fact, the successful database save SHALL persist its recipe update and pending search/embedding states together. Existing derived state SHALL have its embedding fingerprint cleared; absent derived state SHALL be initialized pending. This SHALL NOT establish completed indexing.

#### Scenario: Invalidate existing derived recipe state
- **WHEN** an existing recipe with search-derived state receives a supported non-null PATCH and database save succeeds
- **THEN** the changed recipe is saved with search and embedding states pending and cleared embedding fingerprint

#### Scenario: Initialize absent derived recipe state
- **WHEN** a supported non-null PATCH succeeds for a recipe without search-derived state
- **THEN** pending derived state is created in the same database save as the recipe update

#### Scenario: Persist canonical correction and derived obligations
- **WHEN** a valid current-revision ingredient or basis correction is saved
- **THEN** its canonical facts, protection, content revision and existing durable affected grocery/search refresh obligations are saved together
- **AND** a later dispatch failure does not make the saved correction disappear or establish completed derived refresh

### Requirement: Retain editing and offer another attempt after detail Save failure

When the detail-field update request rejects while the sheet remains open, the editor SHALL remain open with its current drafts and display “Could not save changes. Try again.” Saving SHALL end and Save and Cancel SHALL become available subject to local Save eligibility. Starting another Save SHALL clear the prior error after any required revision reconciliation. Failure feedback SHALL NOT assert that stored data is unchanged or authorize blind replay of a possibly committed ingredient mutation.

#### Scenario: Save rejects
- **WHEN** a detail-field Save request rejects while the editor remains open
- **THEN** the current drafts remain editable, the failure message appears and Saving ends with Cancel and any locally eligible Save available

#### Scenario: Retry after failure
- **WHEN** a person activates an enabled Save after a detail-field Save failure and any required content revision reconciliation
- **THEN** the prior error clears and the current normalized drafts and required captured revision are submitted in another PATCH for the loaded recipe ID

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Guard ingredient and basis edits with the captured revision
At canonical write cutover, ingredient, basis, instruction or shopping-association mutation SHALL require the captured current content revision. Stale or missing revisions SHALL return 409 and apply none of that PATCH. A request containing both canonical lines and legacy ingredient arrays SHALL be rejected without mutation. Other recipe-field-only PATCH requests SHALL retain existing compatibility.

#### Scenario: Another client saved first
- **WHEN** a person saves ingredient or basis edits using a revision preceding another successful correction
- **THEN** the API returns 409 without applying any field in that request
- **AND** the editor retains the local draft and offers current-content reconciliation rather than silently replaying it

- **WHEN** a PATCH changes only non-ingredient, non-basis fields
- **THEN** existing omission, null, validation and response behavior remains applicable

### Requirement: Adapt supported legacy ingredient edits conservatively
A revision-guarded legacy string-only ingredient update SHALL derive canonical lines without guessing quantities. Only demonstrably unchanged unambiguous line associations SHALL retain structured facts. Changed, new or ambiguous lines SHALL retain text with unresolved quantity facts until explicitly corrected; positional matching SHALL NOT transfer amounts.

#### Scenario: Change a legacy string
- **WHEN** a supported current-revision legacy edit changes an ingredient text that previously carried a numeric amount
- **THEN** the changed line does not silently inherit that old amount and unchanged unambiguous lines retain their facts

#### Scenario: Remove or duplicate a legacy row
- **WHEN** a supported legacy edit removes a row or makes its association ambiguous
- **THEN** quantities are not shifted to adjacent rows or duplicated by positional matching


### Requirement: Distinguish failed saving from post-save delivery failure
The editor SHALL retain drafts after validation, conflict or save failure. If persistence succeeded but later response, export or dispatch completion failed, subsequent authoritative reads SHALL expose saved facts and truthful pending work. Retry SHALL reconcile the current content revision rather than blindly replaying a possibly committed mutation.

#### Scenario: Reply is lost after persistence
- **WHEN** a correction commits but its success reply does not reach the client
- **THEN** the draft remains recoverable and a fresh detail read can establish the saved revision before another mutation

#### Scenario: Derived refresh remains pending
- **WHEN** a saved correction has a later refresh dispatch failure
- **THEN** the correction remains saved with its durable pending obligation and the UI does not claim refresh completed

### Requirement: Save explicit manual corrections atomically
A current-revision Save SHALL persist coherent accepted description, independently nullable amount/unit and basis with human protection. It SHALL preserve source evidence and unrelated recipe content. Original numeric amounts SHALL NOT be rescaled when the person changes only the basis.

#### Scenario: Correct an amount and a basis
- **WHEN** a person explicitly corrects a line amount and supplies a positive serving basis using the current revision
- **THEN** Save publishes those draft facts together without rewriting raw yield, unrelated ingredients, instructions or media

#### Scenario: Preserve explicit clearing
- **WHEN** a person clears a previously saved amount or unit and saves using the current revision
- **THEN** that explicit null remains protected from stale extraction and conversion retries without inventing a replacement

#### Scenario: Correct one of several measured rows
- **WHEN** a recipe has 200 g pasta and 100 ml sauce and a person changes pasta to 250 g then saves

- **AND** dated projections and groceries use those saved facts rather than making all rows stale
### Requirement: Retain all drafts through an incompatible client upgrade

An old editor that submits ingredient or instruction content without the new guard SHALL receive an atomic upgrade conflict. The supported refresh route SHALL retain every unsaved field in that browser tab and offer reconciliation against current original facts before resubmission.

- **THEN** no field is applied and its name, description, ingredients, basis, cuisine and meal-type drafts survive the supported upgrade route

#### Scenario: Step draft upgrade
- **WHEN** a step editor encounters an upgrade conflict while viewing scaled portions
- **THEN** the original-basis draft survives, and no projected number is silently saved

### Requirement: Accept fractions and ranges in the ordinary amount field

The existing amount input SHALL accept the supported exact fraction, decimal and closed-range grammar without a new mandatory quantity selector. Validation SHALL retain correctable input. Shopping-name and fixed-scaling corrections SHALL use progressive disclosure.

#### Scenario: English and French input

- **THEN** reopening retains equivalent exact original facts and no display portion overwrites them

#### Scenario: Ambiguous input

The existing detail editor SHALL edit original ingredients and instructions for loaded legacy, canonical and flagged incomplete recipes. # Design

## Context and Existing Ownership

Current `CooksMode`, stepParser/instructionPresentation, RecipeService instruction PATCH and shared serving projection own reading/editing. The current cooking requirement explicitly leaves all step amounts original; this companion replaces that limitation. Reuse stable original sections/steps and the foundation's contentRevision; no separate step quantity store.

## Decisions and Tradeoffs

Use [shared bindings](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md) for mention, whole, absolute, fraction, remainder, fixed and per-item roles. Spans are UTF-16 half-open with expected text and exact text/content revisions; Unicode boundaries and duplicate occurrences must be tested. Structured segments could avoid offsets but would force a richer editor/import rewrite; validated spans fit the existing ordinary text editor. An invalid span leaves its original text untouched, not guessed.

Check allocations only in explicit exhaustive same-row sequences. Alternative branches, mentions and reused references never add demand. A numeric remainder requires compatible known uses and correlation-safe arithmetic; intervals are not independent random allocations. One row's invalid sequence cannot invalidate other proven bindings. Fixed and per-item semantics need explicit evidence.

## First Observable Slice

Four-portion 200 g pasta plus confirmed whole-use text → Edit original total to 250 → dated eight displays 500 g in checklist and step while groceries count 500 g once. It crosses canonical guarded PATCH, generated client, projection/API/PostgreSQL, actual Home → detail → Cook and stateful mocks; no provider calls. Follow with total oil 2 tbsp split 1+1, double to two 2 tbsp steps and total demand 4 tbsp.

## State, Concurrency and Recovery

Ingredient and instruction edits share expectedConten…27 tokens truncated…y wording original and readable without a routine uncertainty notice; keep unaffected valid steps projected. Do not show per-step badges or blanket warning for every unmeasured ingredient. Missing basis leaves original text and correction access; cooking and allowed completion remain available. Preserve time/temperature/equipment, source access, supported sections, both reading modes, focus and the phone/tablet roles described below.

## Approved allocation correction

Alex approved the rule: if original total changes 200→250 g and an explicit partial use is 50 g, retain 50 g original (75 g at portion factor 1.5). Do not redistribute it to 62.5 g original. Relative “half” remains half of the corrected total; proven whole uses track that total. Validate affected groups and remainders again; inconsistencies leave affected wording readable and retain correction/source access without a routine uncertainty notice or cooking block. This decision is settled; implementation approval and runtime acceptance remain separate.

See the shared [dependency/conflict review](../canonical-ingredient-correction/review.md) for approval and release order, and [acceptance corpus](../canonical-ingredient-correction/acceptance-corpus.md) for preservation cases. Proposed API/schema details have one owner in [contracts.md](../canonical-ingredient-correction/contracts.md).
